Apple shares on Tuesday climbed to a market capitalization of $5 trillion for the first time, making it the second company in history to reach that milestone.

Apple is the second company ever to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization

Market capitalization is calculated by multiplying a company's stock price by its total shares outstanding. Because Apple has consistently bought back its own stock, the exact share price needed to reach this precise number could fluctuate.

The achievement comes not long after Apple had previously crossed $4.9 trillion in market cap, when it swapped places with Nvidia to reclaim the title of the world's most valuable company. The two companies continue to take turns in the lead. Apple now joins Nvidia as the only two publicly traded companies to enter this previously unseen valuation territory.

Nvidia became the first company to reach a $5 trillion market cap on Oct. 29, 2025, benefiting from strong demand for its GPUs used to train and run generative AI systems. Apple is the second company to reach the $5 trillion milestone, breaking a pattern seen in the previous three trillion-dollar races.

Apple has been locked in a market cap race with Nvidia and Microsoft

Apple became the first publicly traded company to reach a $1 trillion market cap on Aug. 2, 2018, when its stock price (ticker: AAPL) surpassed $207.05 (adjusted for subsequent stock splits). Apple took just over two years to double that figure, reaching a $2 trillion market cap on Aug. 19, 2020, again as the first to do so.

Less than 17 months later, Apple made history again, becoming the first company to hit a $3 trillion market cap during trading on Jan. 3, 2022. AAPL then notched its first closing market cap above $3 trillion in June 2023.

That streak of consecutive records came to a halt at the next trillion-dollar milestone. Apple hit a $4 trillion market cap for the first time on Oct. 28, 2025, becoming the third company to reach that level after Nvidia and Microsoft. Nvidia got there first in July 2025, and Microsoft followed later that same month.

Apple is in the midst of a CEO transition

As always, this milestone is more symbolic than operational. Still, a $5 trillion market cap reflects extraordinary Wall Street confidence in Apple and marks roughly a fivefold increase in its valuation over about eight years.

The milestone comes as Apple is in the midst of a CEO transition. Tim Cook is set to become executive chairman of the board on Sept. 1, with John Ternus taking over as Apple's CEO.

Apple will report its latest quarterly results on July 30.
